data.name: CustomFilter_Text0
data.value: This page demos how to use the CustomFilter and CustomHighlight properties to replace the built-in text matching.

data.name: CustomFilter_Text1
data.value: You can use the property CustomFilter to supply your own matching logic. It names a client-side function that receives the data item, the text the user typed, and the item's display text, and returns true to keep the item in the list. Here the function folds katakana and half-width katakana down to hiragana, so typing あ, ア or ｱ matches all three forms of the same word.

data.name: CustomFilter_Text2
data.value: On AutoComplete and MultiAutoComplete you can also use CustomHighlight to control how each matched item is drawn in the drop-down. It returns HTML, so the function must escape any text it did not create itself, using wijmo.escapeHtml, to prevent cross-site scripting. Keeping filtering and highlighting separate lets both reuse the same normalization function.

data.name: CustomFilter_Text3
data.value: When CustomFilter is set, CaseSensitiveSearch, BeginsWithSearch and IsContentHtml are ignored, while MinLength and MaxItems still apply. On MultiSelect and MultiSelectListBox the property requires ShowFilterInput to be true. On AutoComplete it has no effect when ItemsSourceFunction is set, because the drop-down contents are then supplied entirely by that function.

data.name: SearchDuringComposition_Text0
data.value: This sample shows how the SearchDuringComposition property lets the AutoComplete control filter its drop-down list while an IME composition is still in progress.

data.name: SearchDuringComposition_Text1
data.value: Default (SearchDuringComposition = false)

data.name: SearchDuringComposition_Text2
data.value: SearchDuringComposition = true

data.name: SearchDuringComposition_Text3
data.value: MultiAutoComplete with SearchDuringComposition = true

data.name: SearchDuringComposition_Text4
data.value: By default the control waits until the IME composition is committed before it searches, so no suggestions appear while the user is still composing. Set SearchDuringComposition to true to filter from the text that is currently being composed. The property only changes when the search runs; MinLength, Delay and MaxItems are honored in both modes.

data.name: SearchDuringComposition_Text5
data.value: The property is available on both AutoComplete and MultiAutoComplete.
